newsitem.title: USA: WebSecure says Centennial tie may hurt shrs.
newsitem.headline: WebSecure says Centennial tie may hurt shrs.

text.p: WebSecure Inc said on Tuesday there has been no change in the operations of the company that would explain the recent drop in the price of its common stock, but problems with Centennial Technologies Inc may be hurting its stock price.
Centennial Technologies said earlier today that it may have materially misstated its earnings and it replaced two of its top executives.
Centennial Technologies Inc is a stockholder of WebSecure, the company said.
WebSecure shares fell 3-1/2 points to 4-1/2 on 42,200 shares of volume. The shares have been as low as 2-3/4 during today's trading.
WebSecure, a development stage company offering Internet access and support for secure commercial transactions and communications, went public on December 5, 1996.
The company offered no immediate further comment on the movement in its stock today.
Websecure founder Bob Kuzara said Centennial owns about 6.2 percent of WebSecure and Websecure bills Centennial about $800 a month for Internet service.
The companies have many shareholders in common, Kuzara said.
Kuzara said he his best guess about the decline in Websecure's shares is from shareholders selling Websecure shares to cover margin calls on Centennial shares.
WebSecure had a common board member with Centennial, but the companies severed that tie in June to prevent conflicts of interest, Kuzara said.
All the major investors in the company are in lockup agreements, meaning they have to hold on to their shares, Kuzara said.
"The only stock that's trading is the people who bought in the IPO (initial public offering)," Kuzara said.
